quests.question: The employee who ___ the most sales this month will get a bonus.
quests.hint: The word right after 'who' refers back to 'the employee' - match the verb to that person.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers back to 'the employee', which is singular. The verb inside the clause takes -s: 'makes'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a singular antecedent after 'who'

quests.question: The teacher who ___ this class is very patient.
quests.hint: 'Who' is standing in for 'the teacher' here - keep the verb singular.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the teacher', a singular antecedent, so the verb takes -s: 'teaches'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a singular antecedent after 'who'

quests.question: The scientist who ___ this experiment works alone every night.
quests.hint: Trace 'who' back to the person it replaces before choosing the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the scientist', which is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'conducts'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a singular antecedent after 'who'

quests.question: The employees who ___ overtime get extra pay.
quests.hint: This time, 'who' refers back to a plural noun - adjust the verb accordingly.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the employees', which is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'work'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a plural antecedent after 'who'

quests.question: The students who ___ their homework early have more free time.
quests.hint: 'Who' stands in for 'the students' here, which is plural.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the students', a plural antecedent, so the verb stays in the base form: 'finish'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a plural antecedent after 'who'

quests.question: The volunteers who ___ at the shelter are always appreciated.
quests.hint: Check the plural noun that 'who' is replacing before choosing the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the volunteers', which is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'help'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a plural antecedent after 'who'

quests.question: The car that ___ in the driveway belongs to my neighbor.
quests.hint: 'That' can refer to things as well as people - trace it back to find the true antecedent.
quests.explanation: 'That' refers to 'the car', which is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'sits'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a singular antecedent after 'which/that'

quests.question: The recipe which ___ five ingredients is surprisingly easy.
quests.hint: 'Which' works the same way as 'that' for agreement - find what it refers to.
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'the recipe', which is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a singular antecedent after 'which/that'

quests.question: The bridge that ___ the two cities was built decades ago.
quests.hint: Trace 'that' back to the noun it replaces before deciding on the verb.
quests.explanation: 'That' refers to 'the bridge', which is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'connects'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a singular antecedent after 'which/that'

quests.question: The books that ___ on this shelf belong to the library.
quests.hint: This time, 'that' refers back to a plural noun.
quests.explanation: 'That' refers to 'the books', which is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'sit'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a plural antecedent after 'which/that'

quests.question: The machines which ___ in this factory run around the clock.
quests.hint: 'Which' is standing in for a plural noun here.
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to 'the machines', which is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'operate'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a plural antecedent after 'which/that'

quests.question: The rules that ___ in this building apply to everyone.
quests.hint: Check whether 'that' is replacing one rule or several before choosing the verb.
quests.explanation: 'That' refers to 'the rules', which is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'exist'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with a plural antecedent after 'which/that'

quests.question: The manager who hires new employees ___ very selective.
quests.hint: This blank is outside the relative clause - it needs to agree with the main subject, not the noun inside the clause.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the manager', which is singular; 'employees' (plural) is just inside the relative clause. The main verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The teacher who grades these essays ___ a lot of feedback.
quests.hint: Ignore 'essays' inside the clause and focus on who the sentence is really about.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the teacher', which is singular. The main verb takes -s: 'gives'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The chef who prepares these dishes ___ years of training.
quests.hint: The plural noun inside the clause doesn't affect the verb that comes after the whole clause.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the chef', which is singular. The main verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The managers who hire new employees ___ very selective.
quests.hint: Compare this to the earlier examples - the main subject here is plural instead of singular.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the managers', which is plural. The main verb stays in the base form: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The teachers who grade these essays ___ a lot of feedback.
quests.hint: Focus on the plural main subject, not the noun inside the relative clause.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the teachers', which is plural. The main verb stays in the base form: 'give'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The chefs who prepare these dishes ___ years of training.
quests.hint: As before, the real subject is outside the relative clause, and it's plural here.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the chefs', which is plural. The main verb stays in the base form: 'have'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The supervisor who, despite a heavy workload, ___ every deadline is highly respected.
quests.hint: This time, even the relative clause itself has a phrase interrupting it - trace back to the true antecedent.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the supervisor', which is singular, even with 'despite a heavy workload' interrupting the clause. The verb takes -s: 'meets'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with its antecedent, even with a phrase interrupting the clause itself

quests.question: The students who, despite limited resources, ___ excellent results are truly impressive.
quests.hint: Skip over the interrupting phrase inside the clause and find what 'who' refers to.
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the students', which is plural, even with the interrupting phrase. The verb stays in the base form: 'achieve'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with its antecedent, even with a phrase interrupting the clause itself

quests.question: The company that, despite tough competition, ___ strong every year deserves praise.
quests.hint: The interrupting phrase about competition doesn't change what 'that' refers to.
quests.explanation: 'That' refers to 'the company', which is singular, even with the interrupting phrase. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.grammarRule: Relative clause verb agrees with its antecedent, even with a phrase interrupting the clause itself

quests.question: The book that sits on the top shelf ___ mine.
quests.hint: The relative clause's own verb is already given - focus on the blank outside the clause instead.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the book', which is singular. The main verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Main verb agreement with the true subject, independent of the relative clause

quests.question: The workers who arrive early ___ better parking spots.

quests.question: The professor who teaches this course ___ known for tough exams.
quests.hint: Again, look past the completed relative clause to the main subject.

quests.question: The employees who work in the department that handles customer complaints ___ specialized training.

quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the true main subject, even through nested relative clauses with multiple distractor nouns

quests.question: The director who oversees the teams that build our software products ___ over a decade of experience.
quests.hint: Even with two clauses stacked together, only the very first noun is the true subject.
quests.explanation: The true main subject is 'the director', which is singular, despite the plural nouns nested inside the sentence. The verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the true main subject, even through nested relative clauses with multiple distractor nouns

quests.question: The reports that were prepared by the analysts who joined last month ___ under review.
quests.hint: Trace back past both clauses to find what the sentence is really about.
quests.explanation: The true main subject is 'the reports', which is plural, despite the singular-sounding details nested inside. The verb stays in the base form: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the true main subject, even through nested relative clauses with multiple distractor nouns

quests.question: The scientist who published this study ___ well-known in her field.
quests.hint: Bring back the basic relative-clause rule: find the main subject outside the clause.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the scientist', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The employees who requested time off ___ approval from their manager.
quests.hint: Focus on the plural main subject here, not any noun inside the clause.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the employees', which is plural. The verb stays in the base form: 'need'.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause

quests.question: The teacher who grades these papers, despite a very busy schedule, ___ detailed comments on each one.

quests.explanation: The main subject is 'the teacher', which is singular. The relative clause 'who grades these papers' and the phrase 'despite a very busy schedule' are both extra detail. The main verb takes -s: 'gives'.
quests.grammarRule: Main verb agreement with the true subject, independent of the relative clause, even with an added interrupting phrase
